newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT - India steady after Wednesday's gains.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT - India steady after Wednesday's gains.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts (GDRs) were steady in London after strong gains on Wednesday despite a strong domestic market on Thursday.
"The market opened firm but came off later as some stock came out and that did spook the market a bit, but the stock was all absorbed," said a trader on Thursday.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index closed up 0.51 points, 0.72 percent, at 71.65 points, with the premium over the local market at 23.88 percent compared with yesterday's 24.46 percent.
"In time all the stock was placed and the market closed on an uptick," said the trader.
The Capel index had risen 3.75 percent on Wednesday.
The Bombay Stock Exchange 30-share index ended at its day high of 3,362.39, up 73.51 points or 2.24 percent.

Finance Minister P. Chidambaram gave an upbeat assessment of the prospects for industrial production to pick up in the second half of 1996/97 and the government reitrated its promise of further expansion of foreign investment and willingness to review corporate tax (MAT).
The Capel Korea GDR Index ended flat, up 0.08 points at 64.45, a premium of 57.78 percent over the local market after the Korea Composite Index rose 18.46 points, or 2.97 percent, to 639.87.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index ended down 0.52 points, 0.58 percent, at 64.45, a premium of 7.03 percent after after the Taiwan Weighted Index fell 8.67 points or 0.12 percent to 7,010.76.
